title: The Midnight Detective
description: Missing jewels, unreliable labels and witnesses whose stories must fit. Every clue you need is in the question.

questions.prompt: Exactly one of Ada, Ben, Cy and Dee took a coin. Ada says 'Ben took it.' Ben says 'Cy took it.' Cy says 'I did not take it.' Dee says 'Ben's statement is false.' Exactly one statement is false. Who took the coin?
questions.hint: One statement and its direct denial already account for one false statement.
questions.explanation: Ben's and Dee's statements are opposites, so the other two statements must both be true. Ada's true statement identifies Ben.

questions.prompt: An alarm sounds exactly when the window is open or the door is unlocked. A lamp lights exactly when the alarm sounds and the guard is absent. The guard is absent, the window is closed and the lamp is off. What follows?
questions.hint: Work backwards from the unlit lamp using the known state of the guard.
questions.explanation: With the guard absent, an alarm would light the lamp. So the alarm is off, which means both an unopened window and a locked door.

questions.explanation: 507 gives the stated counts for all four clues: none; 5 and 0 with only 5 placed; 0 misplaced; then 0 and 7 both placed. Exhaustive checking leaves no other code.

questions.prompt: Three bags contain only stars, only moons, or a mixture of both. Their labels 'Stars', 'Moons' and 'Mixed' are ALL wrong. You draw a star from the bag labelled 'Mixed'. What do the bags labelled 'Stars' and 'Moons' contain, respectively?
questions.hint: The bag you sampled cannot contain a mixture, because its label is wrong.
questions.explanation: The Mixed-labelled bag must be stars only. The Moons-labelled bag cannot be moons or the already assigned stars, so it is mixed; the Stars-labelled bag is moons only.

questions.prompt: Three perfect logicians wear hats selected from two red and three blue hats. Rear sees both ahead; Middle sees only Front; Front sees no hats. All know this. Rear says 'I cannot deduce my colour.' Middle then says the same. What colour can Front deduce their hat is?
questions.hint: The second person can use both the first statement and the hat they see.
questions.explanation: Rear's uncertainty rules out two red hats ahead. If Front were red, Middle would therefore know their own hat was blue; Middle's uncertainty tells Front that Front is blue.

questions.prompt: Ada, Ben, Cy and Dee each always tell the truth or always lie. Ada: 'Ben and Cy are the same type.' Ben: 'Dee is a liar.' Cy: 'Ada and Dee are different types.' Dee: 'Ada and Ben are both truthful.' Who is the only truth-teller?
questions.hint: First test whether the last speaker could be truthful; then follow the consequences.
questions.explanation: Dee cannot be truthful: that would make Ben truthful while Ben calls Dee a liar. Thus Ben is truthful; Dee's false claim then makes Ada a liar, and Cy's claim makes Cy a liar too.
